title: Palette variation
description: Every Pokémon's colours turn a little by its PID's second byte (docs/paperwhite2/design/palette-variation.md): its battle, summary, PC, evolution, trade, hatching and follower sprites, normal and shiny alike. The low nibble turns the hue by one of 16 steps across the hue range; two bits each pick one of 4 steps of the saturation and brightness ranges. Greys, white, black and the transparent colour never change. tools/paperwhite2/palette_variation.py checks the file and writes it into paperwhite2/palette_variation_config.h for src/paperwhite2/main/paperwhite2_palette_variation.c.

enabled.description: Off, every Pokémon has its species' own colours

hue_degrees.description: How far the hue turns at most, either way, in degrees: 16 steps from minus this to plus this. On the DS's 5 bits a channel a strong colour shows a step of about 2 degrees, a pale one needs more

brightness_percent.description: How much brighter or darker at most, in percent: 4 steps from minus this to plus this, scaled by each colour's saturation, so greys keep theirs. Below about 4 the 5-bit channels round most of it away

saturation_percent.description: How much more or less saturated at most, in percent: 4 steps from minus this to plus this. Below about 5 the 5-bit channels round most of it away

species.description: The species whose variation isn't full strength, each listed once: 0 turns it off (a species whose colours mean something, as Kecleon's), 50 halves every range. Its forms, Arceus's plates among them, take the species' strength

strength.description: The share of every range, in percent
